a.text: No one can be told what a battlefield is. You have to see it for yourself.

My friends and I spent a lot of time in Norport's video shop watching old movies, many of them war movies. There were story of heroes, but also stories of terror, depicted by directors with a sadistic streak.
I remembered that the four of us all had nightmares that night.
Even now, I seem to be drifting in a dream.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: We took on a few soldiers who were still breathing when we passed through that valley. Oh, and the survivors have caught up to our column.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: They're all Infected. As they should be, after spending a night in a corpse-filled crater.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You did disinfect properly, didn't you? You could have gotten Active Originium dust on you.

a.text: Where are we, Hannah?
I'm a little...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Don't worry, I have experience with large-scale Active Originium zones from my time in County Hillock.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We undertook the cleanup according to SOP.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The soldiers were conscripts under the Duke of Ashworth. They said that their company simply pulled out after the battle, without rescuing the wounded or cleaning up the battlefield.

a.text: Horn? Is Hannah angry at me because I acted on my own?
Why is she ignoring me?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: He said he had a friend who had been crying for help by a shallow puddle all night. Couldn't turn himself over because his legs were injured.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: He had drowned by the time we found him.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The puddle was ankle-deep. He would have survived if someone had just flipped him over.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I examined the area. Looks like they marched into a Royal Court trap. Some Sarkaz mercenaries must have sacrificed themselves by acting as bait.

a.text: There's something on my chest?
I can't breathe... Morgan... Morgan?
I feel something hot roiling in my chest.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: But... how could they have gone down without a fight?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That's not surprising. Other than the strongest dukes, professional soldiers make up only a quarter of the armies of the other ducal armies, at best.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Most Victorian soldiers are conscripted, sent into battle after only a few months of basic training on how to use a crossbow or Arts Unit.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Frankly, if not for this war, the officers and soldiers may never have spoken to each other their entire lives.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina wouldn't like to hear it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I hate this. How could you trust your back to someone whom you don't trust?

a.text: Why does nobody hear me?
I feel the taste of iron in my mouth, something boiling, rushing up my throat.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mother never answered my questions. She said I would find the answer, someday—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: *Cough*... argh!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Take it easy, Morgan... my neck... I can't breathe...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Sorry, got excited. You had been unconscious for two days.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You were running a fever. At least the wound on your chest was healing well, otherwise we would have been even more worried.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Where are we...? We aren't in Chetleigh anymore, are we?

a.text: They are silent. What happened?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Ahem... Maybe I should explain.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We pulled out two days ago. We're back to our original encampment.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: At Horn's advice, we pulled out as quickly as possible before the Duke of Gododdin's fleet entered Chetleigh, avoiding direct contact with the reinforcements.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...Horn?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We have a lot of... complicated circumstances. It's going to cause a lot of complications if we establish official communications with the dukes' troops.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I've talked about this with Misery, and the others support what we're doing.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: While we still have troops formerly under the command of Duke Windermere, their military ID has expired, and there's a high risk of 'friendly fire'.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Well, not so much expired as no longer recognized...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: No need to mince words about the nobles' dirty deeds.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: It's the same deal as gangs fighting for territory.

a.text: Indra's right.
Since when did the war become like this?
We could give help to where we can see, but what about the places beyond?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...What's the situation?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Some have chosen to join Duke Gododdin's forces and continue the fight. Gododdin's officers didn't even say anything about the Infected. The majority have chosen to stay with us, however.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: They trust us. Or should I say, they trust you. We won! Morale is really high right now.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: They're even joking about the old conflicts now.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We did it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Your plan worked. We made it. It's very possible that no one will ever know the sacrifices we made...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's just one small victory in a greater war.

a.text: I look at Delphine's tired face. A great burden has weighed upon her heart ever since she was left behind by the battleships.
But now, I see a rare smile on her face.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But we saved Chetleigh, Vina.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Yes, we did.

a.text: My brain tells me that I should be relieved or happy.
But I can't do it. I'm afraid to know how many stayed behind in that building, never to leave it.
Everything that happened there seems like a dream.
Is this what victory feels like? It's so weighty.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Would things have gotten so bad if everyone was fully committed to fighting for Victoria from the very beginning?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, they all firmly believe that they are fighting for Victoria.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's the other way round. Things have already spiraled out of control. Therefore...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We're fighting for ourselves now.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Siege, one of the survivors from Chetleigh has brought us a surprise.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: His family collected Gaulish artifacts, and his father once picked up a little Victorian object from Lingones's former route.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: It wasn't anything valuable, so it has been sitting in a warehouse for a long time. He gave it to us before we left as a gift of gratitude, and Horn recognized it immediately.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: This is an IFF beacon used in IFVs. It emits a signal that allows Victorian armies to identify the bearer's affiliation.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It contains a military identification code?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Yes. This black box belonged to the Victorian Army. I'm familiar with the symbol on it.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But I thought that the unit that it once belonged to no longer exists, lost in the ruins of Gaul—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: —the Exemplars.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: A unit of legend, predecessor to Tempest Platoon. This thing took a long journey back to Victoria.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Back to us.

a.text: 'The Exemplars'...
The present dukes may not recognize this ancient unit. At best, it might prevent direct artillery strikes.
But the more important thing is...
The mission of the unit was inscribed inside the box.
The Exemplars
'We make miracles.'

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Consider it a gift from fate.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What's this...? The beacon that Lieutenant Shearer left us has picked up a signal.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Shearer?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Lady Delphine, there has been a change of circumstances at Irnclad Galavae...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: We are approaching your position now. ETA in one hour.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Be prepared for unhappy news... and a guest who insists on seeing you.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Your wounds! What a shoddy work of first aid!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: It may look like the wounds have closed, but the inflammation wasn't effectively treated, which explains the fever.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: With serious wounds like these, it's important that they're treated by a doctor and all vital signs monitored, reducing the chance of lingering after-effects.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You're fortunate that it was a piece of metal, not Originium crystal. When you're dealing with Sarkaz witchcraft devices, even the slightest touch could be infectious.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Even if it wasn't directly caused by Originium, there was a high risk of infection given the circumstances. It's incredible that your blood Originium levels still remain at normal levels.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You really should thank your lucky stars.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Well, it was a chaotic situation, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: At least I'm alive. It pays to have a strong constitution.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Fine. Lady Delphine has explained what happened.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: It was a battle worthy of study in the war colleges, given the difference in strength between the two sides. Most of the people on your side weren't even regulars...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Oh? Should I be sad that no one will remember what we did?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You're wrong on that, Siege.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I'll remember. The soldiers outside will remember. The survivors of Chetleigh will remember.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Most legends are not born from official records.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I didn't know you were the type to say things like that.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Well, I've wrapped your wounds again. Don't try to blow me off with excuses like 'strong constitution', because I'm going to be keeping a close eye on your condition. I'm the doctor in this room.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I'll be checking on your friends too, and the injured soldiers and civilians.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Thanks, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Also...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I suggest you check on that guest. I'm not sure if Lady Delphine is ready to handle her on her own.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I sincerely apologize for my behavior before, and my misplaced assessment about you.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: There is one thing on which I won't budge, however. You're too impulsive and emotional.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You shouldn't be trying to solve every problem on your own. Turn around once in a while, and you'll find plenty of people ready to help.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: *Glug* *glug*— whew!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Take it easy, Aunt Manning.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: The Sarkaz were everywhere on my way here! I thought I was going to die.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Thank goodness that Lieutenant Shearer was tracking Irnclad Galavae, which was how he got there in time to save my life.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: He's a decent man, but lacks flexibility. Those men would never allow him to board the ship.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You said you escaped Irnclad Galavae? What's happening there?

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: It makes me angry just thinking about it! Those damned officers charged into the central hub of the fortress and pointed their swords at me! Marquess Vontaire must be behind this!

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: I found an opportunity to change into inconspicuous clothes and escape. The fortress elevator almost ripped my dress!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sounds like you really were lucky.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: I thought I was just coming along with your mother to see how things were going on the front lines, and to take you home. What's the worst that could happen, safe inside a nomadic fortress? Who would have thought...?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The old Dukes of Windermere would be proud of Mother.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: But you're the Duke of Windermere now, Delphine.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Auntie, you're hurting me... what's that look on your face?

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: The general staff were eager to go back because... they believed the Duke's death was caused by a Leithanian plot.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: You want to laugh, don't you? But they have evidence. Leithanien may not be in league with the Sarkaz, but they undoubtedly caused this situation.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What? Leithanien?

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: The staff are cautious about accusing Leithanian nobles directly, but they have set their sights on the rebellions going on the provinces.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: No one wants to come all this way to fight the Sarkaz, only to return and find the demesne they have defended for centuries has fallen under Leithanian control.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: You're her daughter, Delphine. Your duty will come soon.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Now, let me rest... then we'll leave this place.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Leave? To where?

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: You should not be with these peasants.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Watch your words! Don't call them peasants!

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Alright, Delphine, listen.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: If you really care about them, really think that they're heroes, a part of Victoria...

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: ...Think of how many people like them are there in your mother's demesne.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: If you really want to protect these people, take my advice and seek aid from the Duke of Caster to return to your demesne and take charge.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Perhaps you will have to become a Caster vassal... but you'll be able to fulfill your duty.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: What are you balking at? Did you fall in love with them just because they fought alongside you? You've stopped loving your own subjects?

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Accept it, Delphine... you and your mother have suffered enough.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Accept Duke Caster's proposal, and at least Windermere will be spared from devastation.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Why do you hesitate? Do you really want to be a vagabond forever, leaving your family, your bloodline and your duty behind?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm Mother's daughter. You're right, I have a responsibility, not just to my friends, but to the subjects of Windermere as well.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Why did the Swordguards leave me behind, when I still had such a duty?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: If this was a duty glorious beyond all doubt, why do you come to me in such a condition?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You're right. If Windermere has fallen under the cloud of conspiracy, then I feel both the obligation and desire to do something about it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But I...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We're with you, Delphine. Say what you want to say.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Sorry. I couldn't hold back anymore.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Do you know what we just went through, madam?

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: And you are...?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm not going with you.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: You have a duty!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm my mother's daughter, comrade to these warriors, and nothing else.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Even if I once was... I don't believe it anymore.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I stood here for them, so that their lives would no longer be the playthings of people like you, and I'm not going anywhere until I've bled my last.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Leave.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I hope the Sarkaz don't take you.

a.text: The Viscount's face is a spectacle of color, but Delphine gives her no further chance to speak.
She leaves with her head bowed in the direction of Lieutenant Shearer.
Delphine's expression is calmer than I thought it would be. What she said... what she went through...
It made me think of an old friend.
Delphine did not make the same mistake. Tragedy will not strike again.
But what was the price?
The death of a loved one. A swift betrayal.
Apparently, I was rather concerned how Delphine would react to these things.
Delphine smiles at me. It seems she has settled down.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm fine. Let's go.

a.text: The same thing cannot happen again.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Head west once you leave the camp. If you're lucky enough, you should be able to reach the kind Duke of Caster.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Do you think you can survive without the Duke's protection?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We can, and we will.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Alright... I'm going to Duke Caster. I'll take a leisurely pace. This is your last chance.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: Come with me, and we'll all live.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I won't stop you.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: But the work of Delphine and her mother...

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: No, I'm not the one who's wrong... you're naive, stupid, foolishly believing that you're right.

steps.name: Exhausted Viscount
steps.text: So be it.

a.text: I see her off on a vehicle not meant for rough terrain, leaving under the cover of darkness with a small escort.
I turn around to look at our group.
Hundreds, thousands of eyes converge upon a single spot. Some are soldiers laughing with each other, others are civilians, celebrating.
The camp falls silent.
They are waiting for an answer.
Mine.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You heard her. It was undoubtedly an attractive proposal for many people.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We survived the worst of times together, Vina.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But what now? What happens when the morale and spirit that burns so brightly now is worn away by hardship and suffering?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Who will tell them where to go?

a.text: I do not answer, not yet.
...He's here.
A creature with golden mane walks amongst the crowd. He looks at me.
I wanted to see the answer in his eyes, hear a word of advice in these fleeting moments.
But he gives no answers. All he does is look at me, waiting for me to find the answer.
Yes. Perhaps he is not even there.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Lend me your ears.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If any among you still have faith in the proud dukes that are the faces of our Victoria, you should go with that woman now.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No one would fault your decision.

a.text: The crowd rustles, but no one leaves.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: None among you?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is it not our instinct to seek protection from the powerful? It's nothing to be ashamed of.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I would very much like to. Oh how I wish that this sorry sword I carry had the power to protect my friends, such that none among them would die.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She would very much like to. How many times has she cried when no one was watching? Wishing that someone could have saved her mother's life.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You would very much like to. Don't look away, I know you would. The Sarkaz wouldn't have butchered your brother so badly you couldn't even identify his corpse, if the troops that were supposed to escort you didn't flee.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But none among you have left.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You know that those nobles don't care about you in the slightest.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But do you really need to seek the strength and protection of another?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's always been like that for us. We keep worshipping people and things that never really gave us anything, become their willing slaves.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Massacre, infection, besiegement. We survived all that, on our own strength!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We all want to go home. We all want this rotten war to end. But we can't win by hiding.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The fastest way is to give those warmongering bastards hiding in Londinium the old one-two in the face!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If the dukes won't do it, we will!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If no one will take us home, we'll walk home ourselves!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: A gift fell into our laps, a unit ID that the dukes left behind in Gaul.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It was called the Exemplars. They were elites, the will of the nation, with a long list of accolades.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But now, they are nothing more than this little box in my hands.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It has no special powers. But we can take it back to Londinium—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Punch those warmongering bastards in the face, throw this in the faces of the dukes, and tell them—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This bloody land is OUR land!

a.text: I want to go home, to the gym where my friends were.
They want to go home, to the lives they once had.
We cannot rely on others anymore. We cannot expect justice to be served on its own.
I smash my hammer into the earth with all the strength I can muster.
I do not know why I did it. All I know is that I can no longer hold back my anger.
Bam!
The hammer silences all other sounds.
'The Exemplars!'
It's the Glasgow Gang that first breaks the silence.
'The Exemplars!'
Then, they are joined by Delphine.
'The Exemplars!'
Until everyone joins in.
'The Exemplars!' 'The Exemplars!' 'The Exemplars!'

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Say, I had a strange dream—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I dreamed that a golden beast was taking a walk through our camp.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Good omen, perhaps?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Let's hope it all goes smoothly.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Wonder if the Self-Salvation Corps arrived at Brentwood before us...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: We'll have even more hands once we join up with them.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Who would have thought, a few days ago, that we would have our own army?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I kind of like the name the Exemplars.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Are you sure about this though, Vina? Are we bringing all of them back to Londinium?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Very few of them are ready to fight the Royal Court head-on.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: There will be more sacrifices along the way.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'll protect them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Or maybe there will come a day when they don't need anyone's protection anymore.
